result: Mean onset step for widths 16/32/64/128 was no onset / no onset / no onset / no onset. Final FS was 0.03 / 0.04 / 0.04 / 0.04.
notes: Reduced design because the shared machine was overloaded (load ~250 on 16 cores): 2 seeds (0, 1) instead of 3, 600 GRPO steps instead of 1,000, greedy eval every 50 steps on 1,000 held-out programs (seed 12345) instead of 2,000. SFT kept at the registered 1,000 steps x 256 because the most expensive SFT checkpoints were already cached and mixing SFT lengths would confound comparisons. Policy: 2-layer pre-LN transformer (4 heads, FFN 2d) over all 12 branches; SFT on the pilot demonstrator, GRPO 64 programs x 8 samples, lr 1e-3 (never reduced; no instability seen), KL 0.02 to the frozen SFT copy, grad-norm clip 1.0 as in the pilot. 'Final' means step 600. Std is over 2 seeds (ddof=1). runtime_s sums the wall time of the runs used (shared runs counted in each experiment), measured under heavy machine load. Onset resolution is the 50-step eval grid; a run that never reaches FS 0.15 would be counted as 650 in the mean (shown as null in the per-seed onsets). Verdict: supported if the mean onset strictly decreases from 16 to 128; refuted if width 128's mean onset is not earlier than width 16's; mixed otherwise.
